# Instructions for accurately reporting failed municipal water-quality tests to protect the public

1. Start with the inspection records.

completion:
Keep reading.

**Public officials are well advised to seek legal advice before taking any steps described here.**

An effective municipal water system must carefully manage the critical elements in a high-quality water-quality monitoring program. These include sampled point locations, number of monthly samples, sample-collecting staff training, correct use of sampling equipment, proper sample collection, correct use of water analysis laboratories, and timely reporting of the results.

National regulations require that all public water systems comply with the “Total Coliform Rule” that limits the amount of coliform bacteria found in public water supplies. Coliform procedures must identify total coliforms and *E. coli* in all samples. If a public water system takes only one sample per month, each sample may only show the presence of either total coliforms or *E. coli*.
